description: Arthur, Lancelot, Guinevere: the greatest legend of the Western Middle Ages. An ideal of knighthood destroyed by a forbidden love.

hero.hook: The best knight in the world loves the king's wife. Camelot will never recover.

blocks.text: The legend of King **Arthur** and his knights of the **Round Table** is the great mythological cycle of the Western Middle Ages. It is called the **Matter of Britain**: a mix of blurred history, Celtic folklore and Christian morality.

At the heart of the story lies a very human tragedy: the forbidden love between **Lancelot**, the best of the knights, and Queen **Guinevere**, Arthur's wife. That love, praised as a kind of perfection, becomes the poison that brings **Camelot** down.

There is no single author. Between the 6th and the 15th century, the stories pile up. Behind Arthur we can just make out a British war leader, perhaps called **Arturus**, who is said to have held off the Saxons after the Romans left. Around him grow **Merlin**, the fairies and the magic swords.

blocks.caption: Arthur pulls the sword from the stone: the sign of the rightful king

blocks.text: A 13th-century “Round Table” still hangs in Winchester Castle, in England. Henry VIII had it painted to tie himself to Arthur.

During [[the ordeal of the sword]], only the true king can draw **Excalibur** from the rock, or from the anvil. Crowned at Camelot, Arthur founds the **Round Table**. Its circular shape abolishes rank: around it every knight is the equal of his neighbor, the king included.

sections.title: The sources of the myth: between history and Celtic folklore

blocks.text: Little by little, the fighting gives way to a spiritual quest: the **Holy Grail**. A magic dish in the old Celtic texts, it becomes in the 12th century the chalice of Christ. Inner purity counts as much as strength.

blocks.caption: The quest for the Grail turns the Round Table into a spiritual adventure

blocks.text: The word “grail” came from Old French and at first meant a wide dish for serving meat, not a precious cup.

At the table, the [[Siege Perilous]] waits for the knight who is destined for it. Only **Galahad**, **Perceval** and **Bors** reach the Grail. **Lancelot of the Lake**, “the best knight in the world,” fails: his love for Guinevere makes him unworthy of the divine vision.

sections.title: The quest for the Grail and a spiritual turn

blocks.text: The love of Lancelot and Guinevere is the very model of [[medieval courtly love (fin'amor)]]: the knight puts himself at the service of his lady. But Guinevere is the wife of his overlord. The betrayal is not just a matter of marriage. It is feudal.

blocks.caption: Lancelot and Guinevere: the love that breaks Camelot

blocks.text: **Mordred**, Arthur's nephew or his incestuous son depending on the version, reveals the affair. Arthur condemns Guinevere to the stake. Lancelot saves her, but in the fighting he kills the brothers of **Gawain**. The Round Table splits apart: civil war, and the end of the utopia.

sections.title: Guinevere's betrayal and the tearing of the order

blocks.text: At **Camlann**, Arthur kills Mordred and takes a mortal wound. Excalibur is given back to the Lady of the Lake. Guinevere ends her life in a convent, Lancelot as a hermit. Arthur, they say, sails for the island of **Avalon**.
He becomes the [[Rex Quondam Rexque Futurus]], the “once and future king”: the sleeping king who will return at the darkest hour. Camelot dies into legend, and that is how it survives.
The love of **Lancelot** for **Guinevere** destroys Camelot. The quest for the **Grail** succeeds only for the pure: Lancelot, the best knight, stays outside the sacred threshold.

sections.title: The end of a world and the myth of the sleeping king
